risks: R1: CRITICAL file structure mismatch — spec says `src/api/` but SOPs say `src/root/`. PYTHONPATH is set to `src/root:src`. If code lives in `src/api/`, the import style mandated by SOPs (`import shortener`, `import db`) will fail because `src/api` is not on PYTHONPATH. This is a direct contradiction that will break either the test runner or the app at import time.

R2: Static file mount path conflict — `GET /` serves `static/index.html` and `GET /{code}` is a catch-all path parameter. Without careful route ordering in FastAPI, `GET /links` and `GET /` will be swallowed by the `/{code}` route and return 404. FastAPI matches routes in declaration order, so this is solvable but fragile and unspecified.

R3: `secrets.token_urlsafe(4)` produces codes containing `-` and `_` characters. These are valid in URLs but the `/{code}` route doesn't constrain the path parameter regex. No validation on the `code` column format — codes with special chars could cause subtle issues.
R4: Collision retry with max 5 attempts — the spec doesn't define behavior when all 5 attempts fail. An unhandled exception will bubble as a 500. Should be a well-defined error response.

R5: `original_url UNIQUE` constraint means concurrent inserts of the same URL will race. One will succeed, one will raise IntegrityError. The code must catch this and SELECT the existing row — but the spec doesn't mention this.

R6: `psycopg2` connection lifecycle is unspecified. `get_conn()` could return a new connection per call (expensive), use a module-level singleton (not thread-safe with uvicorn workers), or use a connection pool. Divergent implementations guaranteed.

R7: Test database teardown strategy is unspecified. `conftest.py` 'creates test DB schema, yields TestClient, teardown' — but does teardown mean TRUNCATE between tests, DROP the table, or DROP the database? Test isolation depends on this.

R8: No input validation specified for the URL in `POST /shorten`. No max length, no scheme validation (http/https), no protection against javascript: URIs. Different engineers will make different choices.

R9: The uvicorn command `uvicorn src.api.main:app` uses Python dotted-path import, implying CWD is project root. But the SOP import style forbids `from src.api import ...`. These are only compatible if PYTHONPATH includes `src/api/`, in which case the uvicorn command needs adjustment. Contradictory.
R10: `GET /links` returns all links with no pagination. Acceptable for demo but a scalability concern.
ambiguities: A1: CRITICAL — The file structure says `src/api/` but the SOPs reference `src/root/` and set PYTHONPATH to `src/root:src`. Which directory name is canonical? This must be resolved before implementation begins.

A2: The uvicorn command is `uvicorn src.api.main:app` which implies Python dotted-path import from the project root. But the SOP import style forbids `from src.api import ...` inside modules. These two facts are only compatible if PYTHONPATH includes `src/api/` (or `src/root/`), in which case the uvicorn command should be `uvicorn main:app`. The startup command contradicts the import convention.
A3: `GET /links` — the response schema shows `created_at` but doesn't specify serialization format. ISO 8601 string? Unix timestamp? This affects frontend parsing.
A4: `POST /shorten` — no specification of what happens with invalid/empty URL input. What HTTP status code? What error body shape?

A5: The spec says 'mounts static/' but the file structure puts the HTML at `src/static/index.html`. The mount path in FastAPI needs to resolve to the correct filesystem path relative to the running process. Is the CWD the project root or `src/`?

A6: `short_code VARCHAR(6)` — `secrets.token_urlsafe(4)[:6]` can produce codes shorter than 6 chars (token_urlsafe(4) yields 6 chars, but edge cases exist with padding). Actually `token_urlsafe(4)` produces exactly 6 base64url chars with no padding, so this is fine — but it's worth verifying.

A7: No CORS configuration mentioned. If the frontend is served from the same origin via StaticFiles mount this is fine, but if anyone tries to call the API from a different origin it will fail silently.

A8: Connection string format — the spec uses `postgresql://` scheme which psycopg2 expects as `postgresql://` or `postgres://`. No ambiguity per se, but if a `postgres://` URL is provided (common with Heroku-style platforms), psycopg2 handles it. Just noting the assumption.
questions: Q1: The file structure specifies `src/api/` but SOPs specify `src/root/` with PYTHONPATH set accordingly. Which is the correct directory name? This is a blocking inconsistency.

Q2: Should the uvicorn startup command use the dotted path `src.api.main:app` (implying CWD is project root, no PYTHONPATH manipulation) or `main:app` (implying PYTHONPATH includes the module directory)? These require different import styles.
Q3: What should `POST /shorten` return for invalid input (empty string, non-URL, missing field)? Specifically: HTTP status code and error body format.
Q4: Should `get_conn()` use a connection pool (e.g., psycopg2.pool) or create a new connection per request? Connection pooling is not a third-party library — it's built into psycopg2.
Q5: When all 5 collision retries are exhausted in code generation, what HTTP status should be returned? 500 with a specific error message, or 503 Service Unavailable?
Q6: For `created_at` serialization in `GET /links`, should it be ISO 8601 string (e.g., `2024-01-15T10:30:00Z`) or is any JSON-serializable format acceptable?
assumptions: ASSUME-1: The directory is `src/api/` as stated in the file structure (not `src/root/` from SOPs). PYTHONPATH will be adjusted to `src/api:src` and the import style from SOPs will be followed (i.e., `import db`, `import config`, etc.). The uvicorn command will need adjustment to match.
ASSUME-2: `POST /shorten` with missing or empty `url` field returns HTTP 422 (FastAPI's default Pydantic validation) or HTTP 400 with `{"detail": "..."}` body.
ASSUME-3: `get_conn()` creates a new connection per call. No connection pooling. Acceptable for a demo-scale service.
ASSUME-4: If all 5 collision retries fail, raise an HTTPException with status 500 and a descriptive message.
ASSUME-5: `created_at` is serialized as ISO 8601 string in UTC.
ASSUME-6: No URL validation beyond checking non-empty string. No scheme enforcement (http/https).

ASSUME-7: The `/{code}` route uses a regex-constrained path parameter (e.g., `{code:path}` or length constraint) OR routes are declared in order: `/`, `/links`, `/shorten` before `/{code}` to avoid route shadowing.
ASSUME-8: Test teardown TRUNCATEs the `links` table between tests for isolation, but does not DROP/recreate the schema.
ASSUME-9: The race condition on duplicate `original_url` insert is handled by catching `psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation` and falling back to a SELECT.
ASSUME-10: Static files are mounted at `/static` and `GET /` is a separate route that returns `FileResponse('src/static/index.html')` or equivalent, not a catch-all static mount at `/`.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `POST /shorten` with a valid URL returns HTTP 200 with JSON body containing `short_url` and `code` fields. `short_url` is a full URL ending with the 6-char code.
AC2: `POST /shorten` with the same URL twice returns the same `code` both times (idempotent).
AC3: `POST /shorten` with concurrent duplicate URL submissions does not raise an unhandled exception (race condition handled).
AC4: `GET /{code}` with a valid code returns HTTP 307 with `Location` header pointing to the original URL.
AC5: `GET /{code}` atomically increments `hit_count` — verified by checking DB state after the redirect (per SOP).
AC6: `GET /{code}` with a non-existent code returns HTTP 404.
AC7: `GET /links` returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array where each element has `code`, `original_url`, `created_at`, and `hit_count` fields.
AC8: `GET /` returns HTTP 200 and serves the HTML content of `static/index.html`.
AC9: `GET /links` is not intercepted by the `/{code}` catch-all route (route ordering is correct).
AC10: All 4 endpoints have at least one passing pytest test against a real PostgreSQL database (no mocks).
AC11: All DB queries use parameterised queries — no string interpolation/f-strings in SQL.
AC12: All public functions have type annotations.
AC13: Short code generation retries up to 5 times on collision before failing.
AC14: `migrations/001_init.sql` contains the CREATE TABLE statement and can be run idempotently or at least without error on first run.
AC15: The frontend (`index.html`) contains a form that POSTs to `/shorten`, displays the result, and shows a table of all links refreshed after each submission.
AC16: No third-party dependencies beyond FastAPI, uvicorn, psycopg2-binary, pytest, httpx.
AC17: Each source file is under 200 lines.
AC18: Sibling module imports use direct names (`import db`, not `from src.api import db`) per SOP.

user_answers.Q1: The file structure specifies `src/ap: Use src/root/ as specified in SOPs. All imports must be direct: import shortener, import db, import config. Never from src import or from root import.
user_answers.Q2: Should the uvicorn startup command u: Use PYTHONPATH=src/root uvicorn main:app. Modules import each other directly by name since src/root is on PYTHONPATH.
user_answers.Q3: What should `POST /shorten` return f: 422 Unprocessable Entity for missing field, empty URL, or invalid scheme. FastAPI Pydantic validation handles this automatically with field_validator.
user_answers.Q4: Should `get_conn()` use a connection: New connection per request via get_conn(), close in finally block. No pooling for MVP. Use DATABASE_URL env var.
user_answers.Q5: When all 5 collision retries are exh: Return HTTP 503 Service Unavailable with JSON body {"detail": "Unable to generate unique short code"}.
user_answers.Q6: For `created_at` serialization in `G: ISO 8601 string format (UTC): e.g. 2024-01-15T10:30:00+00:00. Pydantic/FastAPI handles this automatically for datetime fields.
